beats.title: B1 HOOK: two texts from Mom, nine seconds apart
B2 RULE: the fridge note (plants: the key loophole, Room 412)
B3 PRESSURE: the warm Mom, the rule as a test, the near-open
B4 COUNTER-VOICE: the private Mom sees the lock, then lies
S4 TEST: the code word (micro loop)
B5 RUNG: the doorbell, the peephole, the light that never clicks
B5 TOP AUTHORITY: Dad, who never posts
B8 TURN: the voucher is in the house
B6 ISOLATION: only the enemy's channel answers
B10 LIFELINE: the hotel landline, under a battery clock
B5 BARRIER LADDER: hook, key, deadbolt, chain (rule spoken back)
T3 RULE INVERSION: the helper's safe place is the threat
B9 PEAK: the closet opens itself (the one held image)
B10 RESCUE: the planted light decides
B11 TRUTH TWIST after safety: it was worse than you knew

items.text: Mom texted:
items.screen: FRAME 0 = COVER. Lock screen 11:40, two banners already stacked and fully readable: "Family · Mom: I'm outside. Unlock the door." over "Mom: Don't open it. I'm still at work." Behind the phone, sharp: our front door, the red EXIT-sign strip under it broken by two feet

items.text: I'm outside. Unlock the door.
items.screen: Punch-in on banner 1 (Family · Mom)

items.text: Nine seconds later:
items.screen: Punch-in on banner 2 (Mom, the private thread), timestamps 11:40 / 11:40

items.text: Don't open it. I'm still at work.
items.screen: Banner 2 held, red edge pulse

items.text: And one of them was right outside our door.
items.screen: Whip to the front door from inside: hall side dark, only the red EXIT glow under the door, two feet breaking it

items.text: Mom's rule is on our fridge. After ten, the door stays locked. Even for her. She has her own key.
items.screen: Yellow sticky note on the fridge: "AFTER 10 THE DOOR STAYS LOCKED. EVEN FOR ME. I HAVE MY KEY. —M"; smaller second line in Dad's hand: "Dad: Lakeview Suites, Rm 412 (back Sun)". "EVEN FOR ME" underlines itself in red

items.text: Hands full, honey. Phone's on three percent. Please.
items.screen: Family thread (Mom, Dad, Nora). Mom: "hands full honey" / "phone's on 3%" / "please"

items.text: So I sent her the rule. Use your key.
items.screen: Me (blue): "Rule. Use your key."

items.text: Forgot them this morning. Check the hook.
items.screen: Mom: "forgot them this morning" / "check the hook"

items.text: Her keys were on the hook, on the red hospital lanyard. My hand went to the deadbolt.
items.screen: Key hook by the door: Mom's key ring on a plain red lanyard. Then the deadbolt thumb-turn, close; Nora's hand reaching in (near-open)

items.text: Don't touch that lock.
items.screen: Buzz. Private thread "Mom": "Don't touch that lock." arrives with NO typing dots

items.text: How did she know? I typed, your keys are right here.
items.screen: Me: "ur keys are right here on the hook??"

items.text: No they're not. They're in my pocket.
items.screen: Instant, no dots: "No they're not." / "They're in my pocket."

items.text: No typing dots. One second. And I was staring at her keys.
items.screen: Punch-in on the empty space where typing dots should be; cut to the keys on the hook

items.text: So I asked both of them for our code word. Mom and I picked it at the kitchen table. We never typed it anywhere.
items.screen: Me, in both threads: "what's our word?" (two whips). Nora close-up on "kitchen table"

items.text: Nora, I'm not doing this in the hallway. Open up.
items.screen: Family · Mom: "Nora I'm not doing this in the hallway" / "open up"

items.text: Marigold. Now put the chain on.
items.screen: Private · Mom: "Marigold." / "Now put the chain on."

items.text: Only Mom knew that. I slid the chain on.
items.screen: Insert: the door chain sliding into its track

items.text: Then the doorbell rang.
items.screen: Front door, shake on the bell

items.text: Through the peephole, blue scrubs. Head down. Too close to the lens to see a face.
items.screen: Peephole POV: the corridor dark except the red EXIT sign; a blue-scrubs shoulder and a bowed head fill the bottom of the lens

items.text: Our hall light is on a motion sensor. It clicks on for anyone, even the neighbor's cat. It never clicked on.
items.screen: Hold the dark peephole; cut on "never" to the strip under the door: still only red

items.text: Then Dad posted in the family chat. Dad never posts.
items.screen: Family thread: Dad's avatar (D, slate) with typing dots; his last message above it, from Sep 14: "ok"
SILENT bubbles (no VO), big punch-in: Dad: "It's really her, kiddo." / "I just talked to her." / "Let your mother in."

items.text: Dad was in Columbus till Sunday. And he has never lied to me.
items.screen: Nora close-up, worried. Behind her, out of focus: the hall closet door

items.text: I can see your shadow under the door, Nora.
items.screen: Family · Mom: "I can see your shadow under the door, Nora." Cut to floor level: Nora's shadow strip inside, the feet outside

items.text: The handle tilted down. Slowly. Then up.
items.screen: Macro: the lever handle tilts down slowly, then back up
SILENT CAPS bubble (red alert style), phone vibrates, door knocks: "NORA. OPEN. THE DOOR."

items.text: I didn't text Dad back. I called him.
items.screen: Outgoing call screen: "Dad · mobile · calling…" with one red End button
Ringback, faint, in the earpiece only

items.text: Two rings and a pause. Dad's old desk-phone ringtone. Not in my ear. Behind me. In our hall closet.
items.screen: Nora's eyes go wide (no blink). On "Behind me": over-the-shoulder, past her back-view silhouette, to the hall closet door; phone glow pulses under it with each ring
SILENCE BEAT 4.0 s: two more full ring cycles from the closet, no VO, music out. The glow pulses, then goes dark

items.text: The ringing stopped. And in the family chat, Dad was typing.
items.screen: Family thread header: "Dad is typing…"
SILENT calm bubbles: Dad: "Don't turn around, kiddo." / "Just open the front door."

items.text: I backed away from the closet and called the hotel number on the fridge. Room four twelve.
items.screen: Walk-back: Nora toward camera, the closet behind her. Insert: the fridge note's "Rm 412" line. Outgoing call "Lakeview Suites · Room 412"

items.text: Hello? Nora? What's wrong, kiddo?
items.screen: Call connects; timer starts 00:00

items.text: His real voice. Half asleep. Where's your phone, Dad?
items.screen: Nora close-up, phone to her ear, whispering

items.text: My cell? It's in my winter coat. In the hall closet. I forgot it.
items.screen: Call screen; cut on "closet" to the closet door, dark

items.text: Then who's typing on it?
items.screen: Nora close-up, scared
Call timer runs; silence on the line

items.text: Stay on the line. I'm having the front desk call your police.
items.screen: Call screen, timer running

items.text: Eight minutes, they said. My battery said two percent.
items.screen: Battery glyph in the status bar flips red: 2%; chip "police · 8 min"

items.text: Who are you whispering to, honey?
items.screen: Banner over the call: "Family · Mom: who are you whispering to, honey?"

items.text: I looked at the hook. Empty. Nobody had come in. I'd been standing right here.
items.screen: Same framing as the key-hook insert: the hook is empty. Then Nora, looking around her own hallway

items.text: Then a key slid into our lock, from outside.
items.screen: Macro on the lock cylinder, the key sound only

items.text: Even for her, the door stays locked. She has her own key.
items.screen: Flash insert of the fridge note: "I HAVE MY KEY" turns red

items.text: The deadbolt turned. The door slammed open against the chain. Three inches of black. Nothing came in.
items.screen: The thumb-turn rotates by itself; the door jerks open to the chain; the gap is pure black; cold air drifts in; nothing is ever visible in the gap

items.text: Get in the hall closet. Shut the door. Don't make a sound.
items.screen: Banners from the private "Mom": "Get in the hall closet." / "Shut the door." / "Don't make a sound."

items.text: Mom says hide in the closet.
items.screen: Nora whispering into the phone

items.text: Nora, no. That's where my phone is. Whatever's typing is in there. Lock yourself in the bathroom.
items.screen: Call screen; on "in there" a fast cut to the closet door

items.text: I ran for the bathroom. Halfway there, my screen went black. Dead.
items.screen: Hall, running; the phone in her hand goes black (battery dead): the landline is gone
Dark hallway; her breath; the closet door beside her

items.text: And the closet door swung open by itself.
items.screen: The hall closet door swings open on its own

items.text: Dad's coat. Nobody in it. But the sleeve was still swinging.
items.screen: Inside: coats on hangers; Dad's grey winter coat in the middle; its empty sleeve still swinging, slowing

items.text: His phone was lit in the pocket, and it was typing.
items.screen: Push in on the coat pocket: a phone screen glowing through the fabric
THE scariest image, held ~4 s, no music: macro on the phone half out of the pocket, Family thread, draft field typing one letter at a time: "turn around nora"

items.text: It typed, turn around, Nora. I didn't.
items.screen: Nora's face, eyes locked forward; behind her (out of focus) the front door, open to the chain, black gap

items.text: Then red and blue light slid under the front door. The gap eased shut by itself.
items.screen: Red/blue wash pulses under the door and across the wall; the black gap narrows to nothing; the latch clicks

items.text: A man's voice. Police. Your dad called us.
items.screen: Front door, three knocks, red/blue light

items.text: Voices lie. So I watched the light under the door.
items.screen: Floor level: the strip under the door, red/blue only

items.text: Click. The hall light came on for them. It had never come on for her.
items.screen: On "Click" the strip turns warm white: the motion light. Peephole: two officers, lit

items.text: So I broke Mom's rule. Chain off.
items.screen: Insert: chain off

items.text: Two officers. And Mom, running out of the elevator in her blue scrubs.
items.screen: Elevator panel arrives at 6; the lit corridor, a figure running toward us

items.text: Baby, my phone died at nine. I never texted you.
items.screen: Insert: Mom's hand holding her phone, black, dead; it reflects the hall light

items.text: But the private chat knew Marigold.
items.screen: Nora close-up, relief turning to fear

items.text: Nobody knows Marigold. We only ever said it out loud, in our kitchen.
items.screen: Slow push into our dark kitchen behind them, the fridge note just visible

items.text: So whatever answered had been in our kitchen.
items.screen: Nora looking back into the apartment, terrified

items.text: Then my dead phone lit up. The private chat. Mom.
items.screen: Her black phone wakes by itself: lock screen, banner "Mom" (same avatar as frame 0)

items.text: Now I know whose voice you trust.
items.screen: Private thread: typing dots for the FIRST time (the tell breaks), then "Now I know whose voice you trust."

items.text: Next time, I'll call from Room four twelve.
items.screen: Second bubble, read in DAD's landline voice: "Next time, I'll call from Room 412." Bookend: phone over the front door, as in frame 0
Hold on the bookend frame; hard cut to black. No CTA, no part card
